transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
The U.S. air travel system is slowly getting back up to speed
after yesterday's nationwide ground stop.
It's not there yet.
Tracking site FlightAware says more than 11,000 flights into
and out of the U.S. are delayed and canceled today.
NPR's Joel Rose reports aviation regulators are laying the blame
for the telecom meltdown on a federal contractor.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the massive outage
that brought the U.S. aviation system to its knees started
with a routine router upgrade by contractor L3Harris Technologies.
This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment.
A contractor didn't meet the moment.
Or the equipment didn't meet the moment and caused the outages.
The Federal Aviation Administration says the work was part of the transition
from older copper wire to fiber optic cable.
In a statement, L3Harris says it is supporting the FAA's investigation
into what went wrong and that it takes the impact on airlines
and travelers seriously.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says there's progress toward
a trade deal with the U.S.
Dan Karpanchuk reports Carney's comments came during a visit to Manila
where he's wrapping negotiations on a free trade deal with the Philippines.
Carney says he and President Donald Trump recently held lengthy
and substantive talks on a trade deal.
Though he says, quote, "We're not yet there."
U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra has also said a deal could be reached
by the end of the year.
The Prime Minister was speaking in Manila ahead of a three-day summit
of Southeast Asian countries where he announced a new
Canada-Philippines free trade agreement.
Carney said it's part of his strategy to reduce Canada's reliance
on the U.S. as a trading partner.
He is also working towards a broader deal that would provide Canadian exporters
with access to a market of nearly 700 million consumers across Southeast Asia.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpanchuk in Toronto.
New Orleans port officials have sued the owner of a tanker
as the investigation into yesterday's crash goes on.
The tanker appeared to lose control, slamming into a river cruise ship
with nearly 200 people on board, some thrown into the Mississippi.
Police, fire officials and Coast Guard acted swiftly,
rescuing around 100 people. Everyone survived.
Eight people remain hospitalized.
Here's U.S. Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham.
We have shifted our operations from the search and rescue
to now working on fully reopening the river
and coordinating salvage operations for the American heritage.
Officials say that paddlewheel boat may take weeks to remove from the site.
After Washington, Moscow and Kiev met this week,
President Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said today
the U.S. is focused on facilitating direct engagement between Russia
and European nations on the war in Ukraine
and preparing for the next round of trilateral talks.
This is NPR News.
It's been about a year since New Mexico became the first state
to offer free child care to every eligible family regardless of income.
And here's Julie Deppenbrock reports demand is outpacing capacity.
Ready? We're going to march on site. Ready?
One, two, three, march, march.
Across the country, there is a shortage of child care workers.
Olga Grace operates out of her home in Las Cruces, New Mexico.
She's been a child care provider for more than two decades.
The pay is really not.
It doesn't go with the amount of work that we put into what we do, right?
It's not valued enough.
According to the Center for American Progress,
nearly half of all children in the U.S. live in a licensed child care desert
where demand outpaces availability.
Still, the idea of free universal child care is taking hold around the country,
as state and local leaders watch and try to learn
from New Mexico's ambitious experiment.
Julie Deppenbrock, NPR News.
In Bangkok today.
Singer Carmel made history with Sobra Sobra,
winning the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest.
The 19-year-old from the Philippines beat 10 competitors.
She says her song was an ode to female empowerment.
The Starship spacecraft is on its way back to Earth, set to arrive this hour.
SpaceX is hoping its 15th test flight lands exactly where it launched
yesterday from Texas in what would be a world's first,
and a key test in the quest to produce a reusable rocket system
for Moon and Mars travel.
This is NPR News.
plus dot NPR dot org.

topics.text: FAA and Transportation Secretary Duffy blame contractor L3Harris for nationwide air travel outage
Canadian PM Mark Carney says progress toward U.S. trade deal, but not there yet
New Orleans port officials sue tanker owner after tanker rammed river cruise ship on Mississippi
Jared Kushner says U.S. focused on Russia-Europe talks on Ukraine and next trilateral round
New Mexico's free universal child care program faces demand outpacing shortage of workers and capacity
Filipino singer Carmel wins first Asian Eurovision Song Contest with Sobra Sobra
SpaceX Starship returns from 15th test flight, aiming for landing at launch site
